questions.q: Let the line $\mathrm{L}$ intersect the lines $x-2=-y=z-1,2(x+1)=2(y-1)=z+1$ and be parallel to the line $\frac{x-2}{3}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-2}{2}$. Then which of the following points lies on L?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{L}_1: \frac{\mathrm{x}-2}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}}{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{1}=\lambda$ $\mathrm{L}_2: \frac{\mathrm{x}+1}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-1}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{z}+1}{1}=\mu$ dr of line MN will be $ < 3+\lambda-\frac{\mu}{2},-1-\lambda-\frac{\mu}{2}, 2+\lambda-\mu>\&$ it will be proportional to $ < 3,1,2>$
$\Rightarrow \lambda=-\frac{4}{3} \& \mu=-\frac{2}{3}$ $\therefore$ Coordinate of $\mathrm{M}$ will be $ < \left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{4}{3},-\frac{1}{3}\right)$ and equation of required line will be. $\frac{\mathrm{x}-\frac{2}{3}}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-\frac{4}{3}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}+\frac{1}{3}}{2}=\mathrm{k}$ So any point on this line will be $\begin{aligned} & \left(\frac{2}{3}+3 \mathrm{k}, \frac{4}{3}+\mathrm{k},-\frac{1}{3}+2 \mathrm{k}\right) \\ & \because \frac{2}{3}+3 \mathrm{k}=-\frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=-\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}$ $\therefore$ Point lie on the line for $\mathrm{k}=-\frac{1}{3} \text { is }\left(-\frac{1}{3}, 1,-1\right)$

questions.q: If the mirror image of the point $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$ in the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1}$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then $14\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
The given point is $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$.

Let, $Q\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ be the image of $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$ and $' O '$ be the mid-point of $PQ$ which is on the given line 

$\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1} = \lambda$ (say)

$⇒ x = 3\lambda + 1, y = 2\lambda - 1, z = \lambda + 2$ 

let $\left(3\lambda + 1, 2\lambda - 1, \lambda + 2\right)$ be the co-ordinates of $O$.

Direction ratios of the line is ${a}_{1} = 3, {b}_{1} = 2, {c}_{1} = 1$

Also, direction ratios of $PO$ are

$\left(3\lambda - 2, 2\lambda - 5, \lambda - 7\right)$

As, $PO$ is perpendicular to the line

$3\left(3\lambda - 2\right) + 2\left(2\lambda - 5\right) + \lambda - 7 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 23 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{23}{14}$

$∴$ $O$ point is $\left(3 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} + 1, 2 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} - 1, \dfrac{23}{14} + 2\right)$

Since, $O$ is mid-point of $PQ$

$∴ \left(3 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} + 1, 2 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} - 1, \dfrac{23}{14} + 2\right) = \left(\dfrac{3 + \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{4 + \beta}{2}, \dfrac{9 + \gamma}{2}\right)$

So, on comparing both side and solving we get,

$\alpha = \dfrac{62}{7}, \beta = \dfrac{4}{7}, \gamma = \dfrac{- 12}{7}$

Hence, $14\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 108$

questions.q: Let ${L}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \lambda \in R$, ${L}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + p\overset{^}{k}\right), \mu \in R$ and ${L}_{3}: \overset{\to}{r} = \delta ( l\overset{^}{i} + m\overset{^}{j} + n\overset{^}{k} ) , \delta \in R$ be three lines such that ${L}_{1}$ is perpendicular to ${L}_{2}$ and ${L}_{3}$ is perpendicular to both ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$. Then the point which lies on ${L}_{3}$ is
questions.solution:
Given: ${L}_{1} ⊥ {L}_{2}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + p\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 - 1 + 2p = 0$

$⇒ p = - 1$

Also, ${L}_{3} ⊥ {L}_{1}, {L}_{2}$

So, ${L}_{3} ∥ \left({L}_{1} \times {L}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ {L}_{1} \times {L}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ {L}_{1} \times {L}_{2} = - \overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

On comparing with ${L}_{3}: \overset{\to}{r} = \delta ( l\overset{^}{i} + m\overset{^}{j} + n\overset{^}{k} )$, we get that $( - \delta, 7\delta, 4\delta )$ will lie on ${L}_{3}$.

Now, for $\delta = 1$ the point will be $( - 1, 7, 4 )$.

questions.q: Let the line of the shortest distance between the lines ${L}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and ${L}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$ intersect ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. If $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ is the midpoint of the line segment $PQ$, then $2\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$ is equal to___________
questions.solution:
Let point on ${L}_{1}$ be $P\left(\left(1 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}\right)$ and point on ${L}_{2}$ be $Q\left(\left(4 + \mu\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(5 + \mu\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(6 - \mu\right)\overset{^}{k}\right)$.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(\lambda - \mu - 3\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- \lambda - \mu - 3\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(\lambda + \mu - 3\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PQ} ⊥ {L}_{1}, {L}_{2}$

$⇒ \left(\lambda - \mu - 3\right) + \left(\lambda + \mu + 3\right) + \left(\lambda + \mu - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3\lambda + \mu = 3 . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $\left(\lambda - \mu - 3\right) + \left(- \lambda - \mu - 3\right) + \left(- \lambda - \mu + 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ - \lambda - 3\mu = 3 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, solving above equations we get,

$⇒ 3\lambda + \mu - 3\lambda - 9\mu = 3 + 9$

$⇒ - 8\mu = 12$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{- 3}{2}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ P ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{9}{2}\right), Q ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{15}{2}\right)$

So, mid-point of $PQ$ is $\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, 2, 6\right)$

$⇒ 2\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{5}{2} + 2 + 6\right)$

$⇒ 2\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 21$

questions.q: Let $P\text{and}Q$ be the points on the line $\dfrac{x + 3}{8} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{2}$ which are at a distance of $6$ units from the point $R ( 1, 2, 3 )$. If the centroid of the triangle $PQR$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + {\gamma}^{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let, $\dfrac{x + 3}{8} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{2} = \lambda$.

$⇒ x = 8\lambda - 3, y = 2\lambda + 4, z = 2\lambda - 1$

Let, $P ≡ \left(8\lambda - 3, 2\lambda + 4, 2\lambda - 1\right)$.

Now, given $R\left(1, 2, 3\right)$ and $PR = 6 \text{ and } QR = 6$.

So, by distance formula we get,

$⇒ {\left(8\lambda - 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(2\lambda + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2\lambda - 4\right)}^{2} = 36$

$⇒ 64{\lambda}^{2} + 16 - 64\lambda + 4{\lambda}^{2} + 4 + 8\lambda + 4{\lambda}^{2} + 16 - 16\lambda = 36$

$⇒ 72{\lambda}^{2} - 72\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 0, 1$

$⇒ P ≡ \left(- 3, 4, - 1\right)\text{and}Q ≡ \left(5, 6, 1\right)$

Hence, centroid of $△ PQR$ will be,

$\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) ≡ \left(1, 4, 1\right)$.

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + {\gamma}^{2} = 18$

questions.q: Let $Q$ and $R$ be the feet of perpendiculars from the point $P\left(a, a, a\right)$ on the lines $x = y, z = 1$ and $x = - y, z = - 1$ respectively. If $∠ QPR$ is a right angle, then $12{a}^{2}$ is equal to ________
questions.solution:
Given,

Equation of line $x = y, z = 1$

$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{0} = r$

Now, let any point on the above line be $Q\left(r, r, 1\right)$

Similarly, for line $x = - y, z = - 1$ we get,

$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{0} = k$

So, any point on the above line will be $R\left(k, - k, - 1\right)$

Now, the direction ratio of $\overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(a - r\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(a - r\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(a - 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now, finding foot of perpendicular from $P$ on line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{0}$ using perpendicular condition we get,

$a - r + a - r + 0 = 0$

$⇒ 2a = 2r$

$⇒ a = r$

Hence, point $Q\left(a, a, 1\right)$

And similarly, the direction ratio of 

$\overset{\to}{PR} = \left(a - k\right)i + \left(a + k\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And again, finding foot of perpendicular from $P$ on line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{0}$ using perpendicular condition we get,

$a - k - a - k = 0 ⇒ k = 0$

Hence, point $R\left(0, 0, - 1\right)$

Also, given $\overset{\to}{PQ} ⊥ \overset{\to}{PR}$

Now, using perpendicular condition we get,

$\left(a - r\right)\left(a - k\right) + \left(a - r\right)\left(a + k\right) + \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(a - a\right)\left(a - 0\right) + \left(a - a\right)\left(a + 0\right) + \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ a = 1$ or $- 1$

Hence, $12{a}^{2} = 12$

questions.question: Let $Q$ and $R$ be the feet of perpendiculars from the point $P\left(a, a, a\right)$ on the lines $x = y, z = 1$ and $x = - y, z = - 1$ respectively. If $∠ QPR$ is a right angle, then $12{a}^{2}$ is equal to ________
questions.explanation:
Given,

Equation of line $x = y, z = 1$

$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{0} = r$

Now, let any point on the above line be $Q\left(r, r, 1\right)$

Similarly, for line $x = - y, z = - 1$ we get,

$\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{0} = k$

So, any point on the above line will be $R\left(k, - k, - 1\right)$

Now, the direction ratio of $\overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(a - r\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(a - r\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(a - 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now, finding foot of perpendicular from $P$ on line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{0}$ using perpendicular condition we get,

$a - r + a - r + 0 = 0$

$⇒ 2a = 2r$

$⇒ a = r$

Hence, point $Q\left(a, a, 1\right)$

And similarly, the direction ratio of 

$\overset{\to}{PR} = \left(a - k\right)i + \left(a + k\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And again, finding foot of perpendicular from $P$ on line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{0}$ using perpendicular condition we get,

$a - k - a - k = 0 ⇒ k = 0$

Hence, point $R\left(0, 0, - 1\right)$

Also, given $\overset{\to}{PQ} ⊥ \overset{\to}{PR}$

Now, using perpendicular condition we get,

$\left(a - r\right)\left(a - k\right) + \left(a - r\right)\left(a + k\right) + \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(a - a\right)\left(a - 0\right) + \left(a - a\right)\left(a + 0\right) + \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(a - 1\right)\left(a + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ a = 1$ or $- 1$

Hence, $12{a}^{2} = 12$

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{ABC}$ be a triangle of area $15 \sqrt{2}$ and the vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-7 \hat{k}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}}=\mathrm{a} \hat{i}+\mathrm{b} \hat{j}+\mathrm{ck}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}=6 \hat{i}+\mathrm{d} \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}, \mathrm{~d}>0$. Then the square of the length of the largest side of the triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$ is _______
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Area }=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & -7 \\ 6 & d & -2 \end{array}\right|=15 \sqrt{2} \\ & (-4+7 d) \hat{i}-\hat{j}(-2+42)+\hat{k}(d-12) \\ & (7 d-4)^2+(40)^2+(d-12)^2=1800 \\ & 50 d^2-80 d-40=0 \\ & 5 d^2-8 d-4=0 \\ & 5 d^2-10 d-2 d-4 \\ & 5 d(d-2)+2(d-2)=0 \\ & d=2 \text { or } d=-\frac{2}{5} \\ & \because d>0, d=2 \\ & (a+1) \hat{i}+(b+2) \hat{j}+(c-7) \hat{k}=6 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k} \\ & a+1=6 \& b+2=2, c-7=-2 \\ & a=5 \quad b=0 \quad c=5 \\ & |A B|=\sqrt{1+4+49}=\sqrt{54} \\ & |B C|=\sqrt{25+25}=\sqrt{50} \\ & |A C|=\sqrt{86+4+4}=\sqrt{44} \end{aligned}$
Ans. 54

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$ and $\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{^}{i}\right) . \overset{\to}{c} = - 3$. Then ${\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$ 

Now, finding $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}$

Now, solving

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left(5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 5 & 1 & 4 \\ x & y & z\end{cases}\right| = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{i}\left(z - 4y\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(5z - 4x\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5y - x\right) = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

Now, on comparing both side, 

$z - 4y = 14, 4x - 5z = 10, 5y - x = - 20 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, solving 

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ 2x + 3y - 2z = - 3 . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, solving the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$∴ x = 5, y = - 3, z = 2$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 25 + 9 + 4 = 38$
questions.source: Must Do Top Qs of JEE Main 2024

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$ 

Now, finding $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}$

Now, solving

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left(5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\left(7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}\right) + 24\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 5 & 1 & 4 \\ x & y & z\end{cases}\right| = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{i}\left(z - 4y\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(5z - 4x\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5y - x\right) = 14\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} - 20\overset{^}{k}$

Now, on comparing both side, 

$z - 4y = 14, 4x - 5z = 10, 5y - x = - 20 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, solving 

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 3$

$⇒ 2x + 3y - 2z = - 3 . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now, solving the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$∴ x = 5, y = - 3, z = 2$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 25 + 9 + 4 = 38$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$. If the angle between the vector $\overset{\to}{c}$ and the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is $\theta$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $\tan^{2}\theta$ is:
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k$, $\overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k$

Also, $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c} = \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2k = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k\right)$

$⇒ \lambda + 4 = - 1, \lambda + {c}_{2} = - 8, \lambda + {c}_{3} = 2$

$⇒ \lambda = - 5, {c}_{2} = - 3, {c}_{3} = 7$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7k$

Now, finding angle we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left|\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right| ⋅ \left|\left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{12 - 12 + 7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{2\sqrt{481}}$

$⇒ sec\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{481}}{7}$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}\theta = \dfrac{4 \times 481}{49}$

$⇒ 1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1924}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1875}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta \approx 38 . 26$

$⇒ \left[\tan^{2}\theta\right] = \left[38 . 26\right] = 38$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{2\sqrt{481}}$

$⇒ sec\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{481}}{7}$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}\theta = \dfrac{4 \times 481}{49}$

$⇒ 1 + \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1924}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1875}{49}$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta \approx 38 . 26$

$⇒ \left[\tan^{2}\theta\right] = \left[38 . 26\right] = 38$
